note: Statements and provenance are from the v3 brief (Section 5). Each rationale is assembled only from the findings of the design requirements it cites (research/design-requirements.md) and is for Ayman to review or rewrite.

principles.title: Capacity is institutional
principles.statement: Support individual educators in ways that make their institutional conditions visible and discussable.
principles.rationale: Assembled from the cited requirements. DR1: educator capacity, not technology, appears to be the binding constraint. DR2: standards specifying student outcomes without institutional conditions act as exhortation.

principles.title: Enactment over documentation
principles.statement: Count only what is enacted and reviewed as evidence; never produce artefacts that could stand in for practice.
principles.rationale: Assembled from the cited requirements. DR6: no included intervention reached behaviour change in practice or patient outcomes. DR7: the risk of ceremonial compliance under accreditation pressure.

principles.title: Judgement before authority
principles.statement: Educators state their own reasoning before the platform's or the AI's view is shown.
principles.rationale: Assembled from the cited requirements. DR3: the only controlled study testing explainable AI in novice clinicians found automation bias.

principles.title: The tool must model what it teaches
principles.statement: The AI coach discloses that it is AI, states its limits and invites critique.
principles.rationale: Assembled from the cited requirements. DR3: the only controlled study testing explainable AI in novice clinicians found automation bias. DR5: foundational AI literacy has the most defensible evidence base; applied clinical competencies do not yet.

principles.title: Claim no more than the evidence supports
principles.statement: Prioritise foundational literacy, and frame applied outcomes as open questions.
principles.rationale: Assembled from the cited requirement. DR5: foundational AI literacy has the most defensible evidence base; applied clinical competencies do not yet.

principles.title: Every element is traceable
principles.statement: Every item, scenario and principle shows where it comes from and its validation status.
principles.rationale: Assembled from the cited requirement. DR8: design must be revisable from Studies 2–3 and the Delphi.

principles.title: Demand comes from accreditation
principles.statement: Make the link from accreditation pressure to capacity explicit without reducing practice to compliance.
principles.rationale: Assembled from Section 1.1 of the brief. Accreditation bodies are under pressure to specify how AI should be incorporated into dental curricula (Study 1); under isomorphic pressure, schools may respond ceremonially.
